prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1100; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured reported a low-speed collision while the vehicle was parked in a supermarket lot. The claimant, who is not represented, gave a first account by phone and said they felt neck stiffness shortly after the impact.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of loss. Requested the police report and a copy of the scene photographs.

Entry 3: Police report received and the reporting officer confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene. The other driver's statement matches the claimant's description of how the impact occurred.

Entry 4: Two independent witnesses were interviewed and both describe the collision as the claimant described it. Scene photographs show damage that is mostly in line with the impact described.

Entry 5: Claimant reported neck strain and was referred to a clinic for evaluation. The reported injury is plausible for a collision of this kind and no earlier injury to the same area is known from the records available.

Entry 6: Claimant called again to add a few small details about the seating position and the timing of the impact. The core account has not changed since the first report.

Entry 7: A neighbor mentioned seeing the vehicle with body damage several weeks before the claimed date. The neighbor's recollection is unconfirmed and no earlier damage to the vehicle is recorded in our files.

Entry 8: Treatment followed a usual course and symptoms tapered off as the claimant improved. Repair estimate reviewed and the cost is consistent with the damage shown in the photographs.

Entry 9: File reviewed. Injury and vehicle damage are consistent with the reported collision and the claimant's account is unchanged. The neighbor's comment is noted but not supported by other evidence, so the claim proceeds to settlement review.
